messages:
Elaine: Quick sync — I sketched a ‘deployment surface / customer impact’ radar for private installs. Want to prioritize features for the next two sprints (onprem + VPC). High-level asks: installer presets, preflight validator, IP-preservation options, KMS/HSM onboarding, zero-downtime upgrade path, telemetry/retention defaults, and a field-friendly rollback. Thoughts?
Devin: +1 to the radar. Tech constraints to call out: offline installer size (customers want <500MB), Windows service install differences, and kernel/quantization compatibility across GPU types. Zero-downtime rollout likely needs shadow nodes + KV sync — nontrivial.
Meera: From product side, we need concrete launch criteria. My proposal: (a) e2e install <30m for default preset, (b) upgrade path with staged canary + <5% request error delta, (c) preflight validator that catches IP/port conflicts and cert issues, (d) KMS integration tested with one major provider, (e) docs + runbook + support playbook published.
Sam: Field/customer notes: NetOps teams keep asking for IP preservation and deterministic egress. They also want a noninteractive preflight report to hand to their infra team. A lot of customers will only accept upgrades during maintenance windows — so scheduling automation + operator rollback hooks are high priority.
Arjun: For the preflight, we can surface a small CLI that runs checks and emits JSON. Example: ```redwood-preflight --target <host> --output-json preflight.json``` It should check: port binding, IP overlap, required routes, KMS connectivity test, disk space. We can iterate on rule-sets per-customer.
Taylor: Field constraints: some Fortune customers are air-gapped — they require tarball + separate artifact verification and an offline preflight tool. Also many expect explicit network handshake steps with support (IP lists, cert fingerprints). That ups the ops burden unless we provide a stable checklist + automation.
Devin: Implementation notes: operator-shim + an optional lightweight sidecar for routing/fallback could let us keep runtime changes minimal. But the shim needs upgrade semantics that don't invalidate running KV cache. Also want to be careful with prefix caching when routing across variants — can affect latency.
Meera: Tradeoffs to call out in prioritization doc: customer friction (blocked installs) vs. engineering effort. Example: IP-preservation + full offline installer = high customer impact, high effort. Preflight validator = high impact, medium effort. KMS plug-in + runbook = medium impact, medium effort.
Sam: Suggest we gate Dedicated/private GA on three things: preflight validator in prod, documented rollback path + canary procedure, and first 3 pilot customers completed. If those land, CS can take customers live.
Elaine: Good. Proposed owners: Preflight validator -> Arjun; Offline installer + tarball flow -> Taylor; Zero-downtime rollout design -> Devin; KMS onboarding -> Meera + Devin; Docs + runbook -> Sam. Can everyone ack?
Devin: Ack. I'll draft a rollout design doc and call out KV sync constraints.
Arjun: Ack. I'll prototype CLI checks this sprint and post binary + schema in the repo.
Taylor: Ack. I'll collect air-gap customer constraints and produce an installer checklist template.
Meera: Ack. I'll capture launch criteria in the roadmap item and add success metrics.
Sam: Ack. I'll line up two pilot customers and draft support playbook steps.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy created for infra:priv-deploy-preflight v0.1 -> staging (job id a1b2c3). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/a1b2c3
Elaine: Next steps: 1) owners to drop a short RFC in #docs by EOD Fri; 2) Meera to update roadmap board with prioritization matrix; 3) follow-up sync next Tue 10:30am to review preflight prototype. If anyone cannot attend, DM me. :calendar: :mag:
